title: Gangster
tagline: From Snatch to Once Upon a Time in America without noticing the water got hot.

levels.note: Pigs, Capone, a Spanish pool and Coney Island.

levels.name: Modern crime
levels.note: Moles, Mr Blonde, a hitman on the run, Carlito, Nino Brown and a bathhouse.

levels.name: The mob
levels.note: Corleones, Henry Hill, Vegas, Tony Montana, Johnny Boy and Prohibition.

levels.name: Around the world
levels.note: Hong Kong, triads, yakuza, Rio and the banlieue.

levels.name: Old-school
levels.note: Robinson, Cagney, Bogart, and Michael Caine in Newcastle.

core.b: Guy Ritchie: a stolen diamond, a bare-knuckle traveller nobody can understand (Brad Pitt), Brick Top's pigs. Cockney chaos.

br.t: Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels
br.note: Ritchie's first. Core on Crime & Noir
Daniel Craig's cocaine middleman wants out
Ritchie back on form: Matthew McConaughey's weed empire

core.b: De Palma: Kevin Costner's Eliot Ness, Sean Connery's beat cop and De Niro's Capone. The station steps.

br.note: Michael Mann: Johnny Depp's Dillinger
Tom Hardy's Prohibition bootleggers. Thin but fun

core.b: Ray Winstone's retired safecracker sunbathing in Spain, until Ben Kingsley's terrifying recruiter arrives.

br.note: Bob Hoskins's London empire falls apart. Core on Crime & Noir

core.b: Walter Hill: a Coney Island gang framed for a murder must fight its way home across New York in one night. 'Warriors, come out to play!'

br.note: Philip Kaufman's 1960s Bronx gangs
Scorsese: Daniel Day-Lewis's Bill the Butcher in 1860s Five Points

core.b: Scorsese: a cop inside the mob, a mobster inside the cops, Jack Nicholson in the middle. Boston accents for days.

br.note: The Hong Kong original. Core on Asian action
Ben Affleck's Charlestown bank robbers

core.b: Tarantino's debut: a jewel heist gone wrong, told from the warehouse afterwards. Mr Pink, Mr Blonde and the rat.

br.note: Tarantino's script, Tony Scott's film: lovers on the run with the mob's cocaine. The Hopper and Walken scene
Rian Johnson's high-school noir with a teenage drug kingpin. Also on Crime & Noir
Tarantino's interlocking LA stories. Core on Crime & Noir

core.b: Sam Mendes: Tom Hanks's Irish mob hitman goes on the run with his son. Paul Newman, Jude Law and rain.
De Palma: Al Pacino's Puerto Rican ex-con tries to go straight, Sean Penn's coked-up lawyer drags him back. The Grand Central chase.

br.note: Johnny Depp undercover with Al Pacino's small-time hood

core.b: Mario Van Peebles: Wesley Snipes's Nino Brown builds a crack empire in a Harlem tower block.

br.note: Denzel's Harlem heroin king vs Russell Crowe's honest cop

core.b: Cronenberg: Viggo Mortensen's Russian mob driver in London, a midwife with a diary, and the bathhouse fight.

br.note: Aleksei Balabanov: a Russian ex-soldier becomes a hitman in 90s St Petersburg

core.b: Coppola: the Corleones, the horse's head, and Michael's slow turn from war hero to Don. The best gangster film ever made.

seq.note: Young Vito and older Michael. Brilliant, but not better

core.b: Scorsese: Henry Hill's life in the mob, from the Copacabana tracking shot to the helicopter paranoia.

br.note: Scorsese's three-and-a-half-hour farewell to the genre

core.b: Scorsese: De Niro, Pesci and Sharon Stone run Vegas into the ground. Three hours of glamour and baseball bats.

br.note: Warren Beatty's Bugsy Siegel invents Las Vegas. Handsome, stodgy

core.w: Very violent: the vice and the cornfield.

core.b: De Palma: Al Pacino's Tony Montana goes from Cuban refugee to Miami cocaine king. 'Say hello to my little friend.'

br.note: Howard Hawks's original, with Paul Muni

core.b: Early Scorsese: Harvey Keitel's small-time hood and De Niro's reckless Johnny Boy in Little Italy. 'Jumpin' Jack Flash'.

br.note: De Niro's directing debut: a boy between his bus-driver dad and the local boss

core.b: The Coens' Prohibition gang war: Gabriel Byrne's fixer plays the Irish and Italian bosses against each other. 'What's the rumpus?'
John Woo: Chow Yun-fat in a long coat with a matchstick, two brothers on opposite sides of the law. The start of heroic bloodshed.

br.note: Woo and Chow again. On Asian action

core.b: Johnnie To: two triad bosses fight for the ceremonial baton. Quiet politics, then terrifying violence.

seq.note: Louis Koo's reluctant boss. Even darker

br.note: To's Macau gangster Western
Korea: a mob enforcer spares a woman and pays for it
Korea's Infernal Affairs

core.b: Sydney Pollack: Robert Mitchum returns to Japan for an old debt, and Ken Takakura shows him what honour costs. The English-language way into yakuza films.

br.note: Fukasaku's handheld yakuza epic: Japan's Godfather
Kitano's yakuza on a beach holiday
Kitano's yakuza war, a body count with jokes

core.b: Seijun Suzuki's pop-art yakuza film: a reformed hitman drifts across Japan in a powder-blue suit. Mad colours and songs.

br.note: Suzuki's absurdist hitman, which got him fired

core.b: Rio's favelas over two decades: a boy with a camera watches his friends become gangsters.

br.note: The Naples Camorra, without glamour
A young Arab prisoner rises inside a Corsican gang

core.b: Mathieu Kassovitz: three friends drift through 24 hours in the Paris banlieue after a riot, carrying a lost police gun. Black and white, furious.
Edward G. Robinson's Rico climbs Chicago's mob. 'Mother of mercy, is this the end of Rico?'

br.note: Robinson's washed-up gangster holds Bogart and Bacall in a hurricane
Robinson's gangster hides in a monastery. A comedy

core.b: James Cagney's grapefruit, his rise through bootlegging, and that ending on the doorstep.

br.note: Cagney and Bogart in Prohibition New York
D.W. Griffith's 17-minute short: the first gangster film. Scorsese list
Raoul Walsh's Bowery gangster. Scorsese list

core.b: Humphrey Bogart's ageing gangster Roy Earle pulls one last job and runs for the mountains. Bogart's breakthrough.

br.note: Beatty and Dunaway rob banks across Depression Texas. Core on Crime & Noir

core.b: Cagney's mother-fixated psycho, a train robbery, an undercover cop, and 'Made it, Ma! Top of the world!'
Michael Caine's cold London hood goes to Newcastle to find out who killed his brother. The bleakest British gangster film.

br.note: Richard Attenborough's teenage razor-gang killer

core.b: Abel Ferrara: Christopher Walken's drug lord leaves prison to clean up New York his way. Neon, nihilism and Walken at his strangest.
The Hughes brothers: a summer in Watts, and a teenager's life of violence that only goes one way.

br.note: John Singleton: growing up in South Central

core.t: Once Upon a Time in America
core.b: Leone's four-hour elegy for Jewish gangsters in New York across 50 years. Watch the full cut.
core.w: 229 minutes, and a disturbing rape scene.

beyond.b: The Naples Camorra with the glamour stripped out. Bleak, and the antidote to everything above it.
Takeshi Kitano's yakuza wait out a gang war on a beach, playing games like kids. Deadpan, beautiful, then very violent.
